svg.text: Nonlinear source → matching surface → actual 3D wave → declared observer
Near kinetic energy K_n, source internal energy U
R₀/a: initial radius; β = p_g0/p∞; κ: polytropic exponent; t: time; ρ, μ, c: water density, viscosity, sound speed.
p∞ = 100 kPa absolute; p_ac and p_f are gauge pressures; Q = 4πR²Ṙ [m³/s]; A_b = 4πb².
E₀: total declared source energy; K_n: near-field kinetic energy; E_a: wave energy; E_μ, E_out: dissipated/radiated energies.
D: receiver volume; τ_f = (2π f_c)⁻¹, f_c = 1 MHz; r_min: nearest receiver distance; h(t): filter impulse response.
Empty-cavity control: Δp = p∞ − p_B; θ = t/(a√(ρ/p∞)); dots denote time derivatives, not spatial gradients.
